## Proof

We compute $\dim H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(k))$ for all integers $k$, where $n \geq 1$ is a positive integer.

**Case 1: $k \geq 0$.**

The global sections of $\mathcal{O}(k)$ on $\mathbb{P}^n$ are identified with homogeneous polynomials of degree $k$ in the homogeneous coordinates $x_0, \dots, x_n$. Concretely, on the standard affine cover, a global section is given by a homogeneous polynomial $F \in \mathbb{C}[x_0,\dots,x_n]$ of degree $k$, and the map

$$H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(k)) \longrightarrow \{ \text{homogeneous polynomials of degree } k \text{ in } n+1 \text{ variables}\}$$

is an isomorphism. (This is the standard identification: a section $s \in H^0(\mathbb{P}^n,\mathcal{O}(k))$ corresponds to the homogeneous polynomial $F = x_0^k \cdot s|_{U_0}$, where $U_0 = \{x_0 \neq 0\}$, and one checks the gluing on overlaps gives exactly the homogeneity condition.)

A homogeneous polynomial of degree $k$ in $n+1$ variables $x_0,\dots,x_n$ is a linear combination of monomials $x_0^{a_0}\cdots x_n^{a_n}$ with $a_0+\cdots+a_n = k$ and each $a_i \geq 0$. The number of such monomials is the number of solutions to

$$a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_n = k, \quad a_i \geq 0,$$

which is the classical stars-and-bars count:

$$\binom{n+k}{n} = \binom{n+k}{k} = \frac{(n+k)!}{n!\,k!}.$$

These monomials form a basis, so

$$\dim H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(k)) = \binom{n+k}{n}.$$

**Case 2: $k < 0$.**

For $k < 0$, the line bundle $\mathcal{O}(k)$ has negative degree on every line in $\mathbb{P}^n$. Any nonzero global section would give an effective divisor linearly equivalent to $kH$ (where $H$ is the hyperplane class), but $kH$ with $k<0$ cannot be effective. Equivalently, restricting to a line $\ell \cong \mathbb{P}^1 \subset \mathbb{P}^n$ gives an injection $H^0(\mathbb{P}^n,\mathcal{O}(k)) \hookrightarrow H^0(\mathbb{P}^1, \mathcal{O}(k))$, and $H^0(\mathbb{P}^1,\mathcal{O}(k)) = 0$ for $k < 0$. Hence

$$\dim H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(k)) = 0, \quad k < 0.$$

**Combining both cases:**

$$\boxed{\dim H^0(\mathbb{P}^n, \mathcal{O}(k)) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle\binom{n+k}{n} & \text{if } k \geq 0,\\[6pt] 0 & \text{if } k < 0. \end{cases}}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
